claim_text: In this Section, the term "pellets" means products which have been agglomerated either directly by compression or by the addition of a binder in a proportion not exceeding 3 (percent) by weight.

claim_text: In this Section, the term "pellets" means products which have been agglomerated either directly by compression or by the addition of a binder in a proportion not exceeding 3 (percent) by weight.
extraction_notes: Mirror of Section II Note 1 — identical text but applies to Section IV chapters.

claim_text: (A) Goods (other than radioactive ores) answering to a description in heading 2844 or 2845 are to be classified in those headings and in no other heading of this Schedule. (B) Subject to paragraph (A) above, goods answering to a description in heading 2843, 2846 or 2852 are to be classified in those headings and in no other heading of this Section.
extraction_notes: Cross-heading priority rule; not a per-tariff-line predicate but a classification meta-rule. SKIP marker; metadata preserved for repair_feedback.

claim_text: Subject to Note 1 above, goods classifiable in heading 3004, 3005, 3006, 3212, 3303, 3304, 3305, 3306, 3307, 3506, 3707 or 3808 by reason of being put up in measured doses or for retail sale are to be classified in those headings and in no other heading of this Schedule.

claim_text: Goods put up in sets consisting of two or more separate constituents, some or all of which fall in this Section and are intended to be mixed together to obtain a product of Section VI or VII, are to be classified in the heading appropriate to that product.
extraction_notes: SKIP-PURPOSIVE: 'intended to be mixed together' — intent reasoning. Composite-set rule handled by GIR-3 verifier path.

claim_text: Where a product answers to a description in one or more of the headings in Section VI by virtue of being described by name or function and also to heading 3827, then it is classifiable in a heading that references the product by name or function and not under heading 3827.
extraction_notes: Heading 3827 specificity carve-out — meta-rule, not per-line. SKIP marker; metadata preserved.

claim_text: Goods put up in sets consisting of two or more separate constituents, some or all of which fall in this Section and are intended to be mixed together to obtain a product of Section VI or VII, are to be classified in the heading appropriate to that product.
extraction_notes: Mirror of Section VI Note 3. Same SKIP-purposive treatment.

claim_text: This section does not cover animal brush-making bristles or hair (heading 0502); horsehair or horsehair waste (heading 0511).

claim_text: This section does not cover cotton linters or other vegetable materials of Chapter 14.
This section does not cover asbestos of heading 2524 or articles of asbestos or other products of heading 6812 or 6813.

claim_text: This section does not cover hides or skins with their hair or wool on (Chapter 41 or 43) or articles of furskin, artificial fur or articles thereof, of heading 4303 or 4304.

claim_text: For the purposes of this section, the expression 'made up' means: a. cut otherwise than into squares or rectangles; b. produced in the finished state, ready for use; c. cut to size with at least one heat-sealed edge; d. hemmed or with rolled edges; e. cut to size and having undergone drawn thread work; f. assembled by sewing, gumming or otherwise; g. knitted or crocheted to shape.
extraction_notes: Definition of 'made up' for textiles — boolean field in O2 schema (made_up).

claim_text: For the purposes of Chapters 50 to 60: Chapters 50 to 55 and 60 and, except where the context otherwise requires, Chapters 56 to 59 do not apply to goods made up within the meaning of note 7 above.

claim_text: This Section does not cover prepared paints, inks or other products with a basis of metallic flakes or powder (headings 3207 to 3210, 3212, 3213 or 3215).
This Section does not cover ferro-cerium or other pyrophoric alloys (heading 3606).
This Section does not cover goods of Chapter 71 (for example, precious metal alloys, base metal clad with precious metal, imitation jewellery).

extraction_notes: Definitive enumeration of base metals — applies to any tariff line in Section XV.

extraction_notes: Predominance rule — O2 must materialize predominant_element. Verifier asserts presence.

claim_text: (b) Powders: products of which 90% or more by weight passes through a sieve having a mesh aperture of 1 mm.
extraction_notes: Numeric definition — uses sieve_pass_pct_1mm O2 field per sub-spec 04.

claim_text: This Section does not cover transmission or conveyor belts or belting, of plastics of Chapter 39, or of vulcanised rubber (heading 4010), or other articles of a kind used in machinery or mechanical or electrical appliances or for other technical uses, of vulcanised rubber other than hard rubber (heading 4016).
This Section does not cover precious or semi-precious stones (natural, synthetic or reconstructed) of headings 7102 to 7104, or articles wholly of such stones of heading 7116.
This Section does not cover parts of general use, as defined in Note 2 to Section XV, of base metal (Section XV), or similar goods of plastics (Chapter 39).

(b) mixed consignments of such waste and other waste are to be classified in heading 8549.

claim_text: Ch.38 does not cover medicaments (Heading 3003 or 3004).

Throughout this Schedule, the expression 'plastics' means those materials of headings 3901 to 3914 which are capable of being formed under external influence (usually heat and pressure) by moulding, casting, extruding, rolling or other process into shapes which are retained on the removal of the external influence.
extraction_notes: SKIP: definition. The material='plastic' attribution is downstream of this; not a per-line predicate.

claim_text: Ch.39 does not cover separate chemically defined organic compounds (Chapter 29).

Ch.39 does not cover articles of Section XVI (machines and mechanical or electrical appliances).

Throughout this Schedule the expression 'rubber' means the following products: natural rubber, balata, gutta-percha, guayule, chicle and similar natural gums, synthetic rubber, factice derived from oils, and such substances reclaimed.
Ch.40 does not cover goods of Section XI (textiles and textile articles).
Ch.40 does not cover footwear or parts thereof of Chapter 64.
Thread wholly of vulcanized rubber, of which any cross-sectional dimension exceeds 5 mm, is to be classified as strip, rods or profile shapes, of heading 4008.

Ch.43 does not cover gloves, mittens and mitts, consisting of leather and furskin or of leather and artificial fur (heading 4203).

Except for the goods of heading 4814 or 4821, paper, paperboard, cellulose wadding and articles thereof, printed with motifs, characters or pictorial representations, which are not merely subsidiary to the primary use of the goods, fall in Chapter 49.

claim_text: Ch.49 does not cover photographic negatives or positives on transparent bases (Chapter 37).

claim_text: Ch.61 does not cover worn clothing or other worn articles of heading 6309.
Ch.61 does not cover orthopaedic appliances, surgical belts, trusses or the like (heading 9021).

For the purpose of heading 6111: (a) the expression 'babies' garments and clothing accessories' means articles for young children of a body height not exceeding 86 cm; (b) articles which are, prima facie, classifiable both in heading 6111 and in other headings of this Chapter are to be classified in heading 6111.
extraction_notes: Body-height predicate not per-line; classification-priority rule.

claim_text: This Chapter applies only to made up articles of any textile fabric other than wadding, excluding knitted or crocheted (other than those of heading 6212).
extraction_notes: KEY rule per sub-spec 04: Ch.62 = made-up textile that is NOT knitted/crocheted OR is h.6212. Uses candidate.heading carve-out.

claim_text: Ch.62 does not cover worn clothing or other worn articles of heading 6309.

Scarves and articles of the scarf type, square or approximately square, of which no side exceeds 60 cm are to be classified as handkerchiefs (heading 6213). Handkerchiefs of which any side exceeds 60 cm are to be classified in heading 6214.
Sub-Chapter I does not cover goods of Chapters 56 to 62.
extraction_notes: Hierarchical exclusion — sub-chapter scope, not a single-attribute predicate.

claim_text: Heading 6309 applies only to textile-material clothing, blankets, bed linen, furnishing articles, footwear and headgear that show signs of appreciable wear and are presented in bulk or in bales.
extraction_notes: h.6309 scope. form='bulk_packed' is proposed enum.

claim_text: Ch.64 does not cover disposable foot or shoe coverings of flimsy material (for example, paper, sheeting of plastics) without applied soles.
Ch.64 does not cover footwear of textile material, without an outer sole glued, sewn or otherwise affixed (Section XI).
Ch.64 does not cover orthopaedic footwear (heading 9021).
extraction_notes: Clause (e). Note: intended_use is an array so both values can co-exist.

claim_text: Ch.65 does not cover worn headgear of heading 6309.
Ch.68 does not cover goods of Chapter 25.
Ch.68 does not cover electrical insulators (heading 8546).
This Chapter applies only to ceramic products which have been fired after shaping.

Articles heated to temperatures less than 800C for purposes such as curing of resins, accelerating hydration reactions, or for the removal of water or other volatile components, are not considered to be fired. Such articles are excluded from Chapter 69.

For the purposes of heading 7019, the expression 'glass wool' means: (a) mineral wools with a silica (SiO2) content not less than 60% by weight; (b) mineral wools with a silica (SiO2) content less than 60% but with an alkaline oxide content exceeding 5% by weight or a boric oxide content exceeding 2% by weight. Mineral wools which do not comply with the above specifications fall in heading 6806.
extraction_notes: Silica composition % numeric fields not in O2 (DSL-gap-deferred).

claim_text: Throughout this Schedule, the expression 'glass' includes fused quartz and other fused silica.

All articles consisting wholly or partly: (a) of natural or cultured pearls or of precious or of semi-precious stones; or (b) of precious metal or of metal clad with precious metal, are to be classified in this Chapter.
Ch.71 does not cover supported catalysts (heading 3815).
The expression 'precious metal' means silver, gold and platinum. The expression 'platinum' means platinum, iridium, osmium, palladium, rhodium and ruthenium.
For the purposes of this Chapter, any alloy containing precious metal is to be treated as an alloy of precious metal if any one precious metal constitutes as much as 2% by weight of the alloy.

For the purposes of heading 7113, the expression 'articles of jewellery' means: (a) any small objects of personal adornment (for example, rings, bracelets, necklaces, brooches, ear-rings, watch-chains, fobs, pendants, tie-pins, cuff-links, dress-studs, religious or other medals and insignia); and (b) articles of personal use of a kind normally carried in the pocket, in the handbag or on the person.
Pig Iron: Iron-carbon alloys not usefully malleable, containing more than 2% by weight of carbon.
Spiegeleisen: Iron-carbon alloys containing by weight more than 6% but not more than 30% of manganese and otherwise conforming to the pig iron specification.
Steel: Ferrous materials which are usefully malleable and which contain by weight 2% or less of carbon.
extraction_notes: Steel definition. Chromium-steel carve-out at higher C% ignored for simplicity (DSL captures primary rule).

claim_text: Stainless steel: Alloy steels containing, by weight, 1.2% or less of carbon and 10.5% or more of chromium, with or without other elements.
extraction_notes: CRITICAL definition — stainless steel. Uses carbon_pct + chromium_pct from sub-spec 04.

claim_text: Other alloy steel: Steels not complying with the definition of stainless steel and containing by weight one or more of the following elements in the proportion shown (0.3%+ Al, 0.0008%+ B, 0.3%+ Cr, 0.3%+ Co, 0.4%+ Cu, 0.4%+ Pb, 1.65%+ Mn, 0.08%+ Mo, 0.3%+ Ni, 0.06%+ Nb, 0.6%+ Si, 0.05%+ Ti, 0.3%+ W, 0.1%+ V, 0.05%+ Zr).
extraction_notes: Alloy steel definition — uses all O2 numeric composition fields.

claim_text: Granules: Products of which less than 90% by weight passes through a sieve with a mesh aperture of 1 mm and of which 90% or more by weight passes through a sieve with a mesh aperture of 5 mm.
extraction_notes: Granule definition uses sieve_pass_pct_1mm + sieve_pass_pct_5mm O2 fields per sub-spec 04.

claim_text: Ferrous metals clad with another ferrous metal are to be classified as products of the ferrous metal predominating by weight.

In this Chapter, the expression 'cast iron' applies to products obtained by casting in which iron predominates by weight over each of the other elements and which do not comply with the chemical composition of steel as defined in Note 1(d) to Chapter 72.
In this Chapter, the word 'wire' means hot or cold-formed products of any cross-sectional shape, of which no cross-sectional dimension exceeds 16 mm.

Refined copper: Metal containing at least 99.85 per cent by weight of copper; or Metal containing at least 97.5 per cent by weight of copper, provided that the content by weight of any other element does not exceed specified limits.
extraction_notes: Uses copper_pct O2 field. Conservative threshold (97.5%, the lower bound).

claim_text: Copper alloys: Metallic substances other than unrefined copper in which copper predominates by weight over each of the other elements.
Aluminium, not alloyed: Metal containing by weight at least 99% of aluminium, provided that the content by weight of any other element does not exceed specified limits.
Aluminium alloys: Metallic substances in which aluminium predominates by weight over each of the other elements.
Zinc, not alloyed: Metal containing by weight at least 97.5% of Zinc.
extraction_notes: zinc_pct not in current O2 numeric set — flagged as gap (extend O2 schema for Ch.79).

claim_text: This Chapter covers only articles with a blade, working edge, working surface or other working part of: (a) base metal; (b) metal carbides or cermets; (c) precious or semi-precious stones on a support of base metal; or (d) abrasive materials on a support of base metal.
Parts of general use as defined in Note 2 to Section XV are in all cases excluded from Ch.82.

For the purposes of heading 8302, the word 'castors' means those having a diameter (including, where appropriate, tyres) not exceeding 75 mm, or those having a diameter exceeding 75 mm provided that the width of the wheel or tyre fitted thereto is less than 30 mm.
extraction_notes: Numeric diameter/width fields not in O2 (DSL-gap-deferred).

claim_text: Ch.84 does not cover millstones, grindstones or other articles of Chapter 68.
Ch.84 does not cover machinery or appliances of ceramic material and ceramic parts of machinery or appliances of any material (Chapter 69).
Ch.84 does not cover vacuum cleaners of heading 8508.
Ch.84 does not cover electro-mechanical domestic appliances of heading 8509; digital cameras of heading 8525.

For the purposes of heading 8471, the expression 'automatic data processing machine' means a machine capable of (i) storing the processing programme and at least the data immediately necessary for execution; (ii) being freely programmed; (iii) performing arithmetical computations; and (iv) executing without human intervention.

Heading 8471 does not cover the following when presented separately: (i) printers, copying machines, facsimile machines; (ii) apparatus for transmission/reception in a wired or wireless network; (iii) loudspeakers and microphones; (iv) television cameras, digital cameras and video camera recorders; (v) monitors and projectors.
extraction_notes: h.8471 carve-out — separately presented peripherals classified elsewhere.

claim_text: For the purposes of heading 8485, the expression 'additive manufacturing' (also referred to as 3D printing) means the formation of physical objects, based on a digital model, by the successive addition and layering, and consolidation and solidification, of material.

Ch.85 does not cover electrically warmed blankets, bed pads, foot-muffs or the like; electrically warmed clothing, footwear or ear pads or other electrically warmed articles worn on or about the person.
extraction_notes: Clause (a). Uses electrically_warmed + wearable O2 booleans per sub-spec 04. KEY rule.

claim_text: Ch.85 does not cover electrically heated furniture of Chapter 94.
extraction_notes: Clause (e). Uses electrically_heated O2 boolean per sub-spec 04.

claim_text: Ch.85 does not cover vacuum apparatus of a kind used in medical, surgical, dental or veterinary sciences (heading 9018).

Heading 8509 covers only the following electro-mechanical machines of the kind commonly used for domestic purposes: (a) floor polishers, food grinders and mixers, fruit or vegetable juice extractors, of any weight; (b) other machines provided the weight of such machines does not exceed 20 kg.

For the purposes of heading 8517, the term 'smartphones' means telephones for cellular networks, equipped with a mobile operating system designed to perform the functions of an automatic data processing machine.
Ch.86 does not cover railway or tramway sleepers of wood or of concrete (heading 4406 or 6810).
Ch.86 does not cover electrical signalling, safety or traffic control equipment of heading 8530.
Ch.87 does not cover railway or tramway rolling-stock designed solely for running on rails.
For the purposes of this Chapter, 'tractors' means vehicles constructed essentially for hauling or pushing another vehicle, appliance or load.
Heading 8712 includes all children's bicycles. Other children's cycles fall in heading 9503.

For the purposes of this Chapter, the expression 'unmanned aircraft' means any aircraft, other than those of heading 8801, designed to be flown without a pilot on board. The expression does not cover flying toys designed solely for amusement purposes (heading 9503).

Ch.90 does not cover parts of general use, as defined in Note 2 to Section XV, of base metal (Section XV) or similar goods of plastics (Chapter 39); however, articles specially designed for use exclusively in implants in medical, surgical, dental or veterinary sciences are to be classified in heading 9021.
extraction_notes: Clause (f). intended_role per sub-spec 04 (high SKIP risk).

claim_text: Ch.90 does not cover articles of Chapter 95 (toys, games and sports requisites).

For the purpose of heading 9021, the expression 'orthopaedic appliances' means appliances for: (i) preventing or correcting bodily deformities; or (ii) supporting or holding parts of the body following an illness, operation or injury.
extraction_notes: Orthopaedic definition. 'Made to measure' and 'mass produced singly' clauses are SKIP-purposive.

claim_text: Heading 9101 covers only watches with case wholly of precious metal or of metal clad with precious metal. Watches with case of base metal inlaid with precious metal fall in heading 9102.

For the purposes of this Chapter, the expression 'watch movements' means devices regulated by a balance-wheel and hairspring, quartz crystal or any other system capable of determining intervals of time. Such watch movements shall not exceed 12 mm in thickness and 50 mm in width, length or diameter.
Ch.93 does not cover armoured fighting vehicles (heading 8710).
Ch.94 does not cover lamps or light sources and parts thereof of Chapter 85.
Ch.94 does not cover dentists' chairs incorporating dental appliances of heading 9018 or dentists' spittoons (heading 9018).
The articles referred to in headings 9401 to 9403 are to be classified in those headings only if they are designed for placing on the floor or ground.
extraction_notes: Floor-placement requirement. Exceptions for cupboards/bookcases/seats/beds (clause a/b) noted in claim_text.

claim_text: For the purposes of heading 9406, the expression 'prefabricated buildings' means buildings which are finished in the factory or put up as elements, presented together, to be assembled on site.
Ch.95 does not cover sports clothing and special articles of apparel of textiles, of Chapter 61 or 62.
Ch.95 does not cover sports footwear of Chapter 64.
Ch.95 does not cover unmanned aircraft (heading 8806).
Heading 9503 does not cover articles which, on account of their design, shape or constituent material, are identifiable as intended exclusively for animals, for example, 'pet toys'.
Ch.96 does not cover articles of Chapter 94 (furniture, luminaires).
Ch.97 does not cover pearls, natural or cultured, or precious or semi-precious stones (headings 7101 to 7103).
Heading 9701 does not apply to mosaics that are mass-produced reproductions, casts or works of conventional craftsmanship of a commercial character.
Headings 9803 and 9804 do not apply to: (a) motor vehicles; (b) alcoholic beverages; and (c) tobacco and manufactured products thereof.
Ch.66 does not cover firearm-sticks, sword-sticks, loaded walking-sticks or the like (Chapter 93).
Ch.66 does not cover measure walking-sticks (heading 9017).
Ch.67 does not cover filtering or straining cloth of human hair (heading 5911).
Heading 6701 does not cover articles in which feathers or down constitute only filling or padding (for example, bedding of heading 9404).

Ch.92 does not cover microphones, amplifiers, loud-speakers, head-phones, switches, stroboscopes or other accessory instruments of Chapter 85 or 90, for use with but not incorporated in instruments of this Chapter.
Ch.92 does not cover parts of general use, as defined in Note 2 to Section XV, of base metal (Section XV), or similar goods of plastics (Chapter 39).
Ch.92 does not cover toy instruments or apparatus (heading 9503).

Heading 6212 is the sole heading in Chapter 62 that may cover knitted or crocheted articles (per Chapter Note 1). Brassieres, girdles, corsets etc. are classified here whether or not knitted or crocheted.
extraction_notes: h.6212 is the knitted-allowed exception in Ch.62 — critical carve-out per sub-spec 04.

claim_text: For the purposes of sub-heading 2204 10, the expression 'sparkling wine' means wine which, when kept at a temperature of 20C in closed containers, has an excess pressure of not less than 3 bars.
extraction_notes: co2_pressure_bar not in O2 (DSL-gap-deferred). Sparkling wine definition.

claim_text: For the purposes of sub-headings 5209.42 and 5211.42, the expression 'denim' means fabrics of yarns of different colours, of 3-thread or 4-thread twill, including broken twill, warp faced, the warp yarns of which are of one and the same colour and the weft yarns of which are unbleached, bleached, dyed, grey or coloured a lighter shade.
extraction_notes: Denim definition. Detailed weave structure (3/4 thread twill, warp face) is SKIP-difficult to encode — accept basic material match.

claim_text: For the purposes of sub-headings 5209.42 and 5211.42, the expression 'denim' means fabrics of yarns of different colours, of 3-thread or 4-thread twill, including broken twill, warp faced.
extraction_notes: Mirror of 5209.42 note (identical definition applies to both subheadings).

claim_text: In this Chapter the expression 'refined lead' means metal containing by weight at least 99.9% of lead, provided that the content by weight of any other element does not exceed specified limits.
extraction_notes: Refined lead definition — uses lead_pct from O2 schema.
